title: Implementation, barriers, and recommendations for further development of advance care planning in inpatient care facilities for people with disabilities in Germany: A protocol for a mixed methods study
summary:
Background
People with disabilities often face challenges at the end of life. Since 2018, advance care planning (ACP) for the last phase of life can be provided in facilites for integration assistance in accordance with § 132g SGB V and billed via statutory health insurance. This is intended to support residents in developing ideas for future treatments. These ideas should be documented for healthcare staff for the case residents are no longer able to express themselves in the event of illness. So far, however, the imolementation of ACP in integration assistance seems to have progressed slowly. It is not yet known what hurdles stand in the way of its introduction, how ACP works in the field of integration assistance and how people with disabilities deal with this new and challenging service.

Aim
The AGREE project aims to answer the question, how ACP has been organized in integration assistance to date. Dissemination and utilization will be examined, challenges and good practices of implementation identified, experiences of counselors and residents explored and effectiveness evaluated. Finally, practical recommendations for the further development of § 132g SGB V are derived.

Methods
Various methods are used in the AGREE project:
- Interviews with experts provide an initial insight into the topic of ACP in integration assistance.
- Structural framework conditions of ACP in integration assistance and experiences of ACP counselors are collected with the help of questionnaires.
- In order to determine the effectiveness of ACP in integration assistance, counseling sessions are evaluated and care pathways are traced.
- The experiences and attitudes of residents in facilites for integration assistance are explored through interviews.
- Focus group interviews will be used to develop recommendations for improving the care practice of ACP in integration assistance.

Relevance of the expected results
The recommendations developed in the project can be used to improve the practical implementation of ACP in integration assistance. In addition, the agreement in accordance with § 132g SGB V can be further developed. This can contribute to improving the quality of care, treatment satisfaction and the quality of life of people with disabilities at the end of life.

interventions.name: a) expert interviews with ACP experts, ACP counselors, leading practitioners (group 1)
b) questionnaire survey in facilites for integration assistance (group 2)
c) online survey of ACP counselors (group 3)
d) qualitative interviews with residents in facilites for integration assistance (group 4)
e) analysis of counseling documentation forms (group 5)
g) focus groups with ACP experts, ACP counselors, health insurance representatives, local experts and association representatives (group 7)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
None.
Exclusion criteria:
No informed consent to study participation; < 18 years; lack of sufficient German skills for study participation
